name: page-tabs
purpose: The second-level navigation strip of a resource detail page: a full-bleed bar ruled at the bottom, its `Tabs` at the page boundary inset, with room for the actions the whole resource owns on the right (a staged-changes `Tag`, Deploy). It is `Tabs` plus the strip and the actions region, so every detail page stops re-creating the same bar.
useWhen: Use PageTabs for the second-level navigation strip of a resource detail page; to switch peer views inside a page or panel use Tabs.
The top of every resource detail page, under the global header.
An account page split into tabs, such as Billing.
avoidWhen: Tabs inside a card, a drawer or a panel → use `tabs`.
Steps of a flow → use `stepper` or `wizard`.
Navigation between pages of the app → use `sidebar` or `navigation-menu`.
related: `tabs` — the tablist it renders; pass one `Tabs.Trigger` per section in the default slot.
`page-header` — the page heading under the strip.
`tag` and `button` — the usual content of the `actions` slot.
bestPractices: Bind `v-model` to the route (or a ref) and render the section below from it. PageTabs renders only the tab list, so it takes no `Tabs.Content`: the page renders the active section itself from the `v-model` value.
Keep the labels to one word where possible.
Put only actions that apply to the whole resource in `actions`; page-level actions go in the `page-header`.
Set `column` to the column the page body uses (`form` over a settings form, `data` over a list) so the tabs start where the content starts.

props.name: column
props.doc: The page column the tab row lines up with: the full width, or the data, form or focused column below it.

props.name: align
props.doc: Where the tab triggers sit in the row: at the start edge, or centred. Passed to `Tabs.List`.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: One Tabs.Trigger per section of the resource.

slots.name: actions
slots.notes: The actions the whole resource owns, on the right of the strip: a staged-changes Tag, Deploy.
